title: A meal in Bhubaneswar
lead: Between the carved stone and the next street, leave a little space at the table.
photo_context: Chhena poda photographed in Puri, 2022. A portrait of the dish, not a Bhubaneswar restaurant or a promised serving.

sections.title: Begin with dalma
sections.text: Lentils, vegetables and spices: dalma brings several ingredients into one quiet bowl. Odisha Tourism describes it as part of a meal and also pairs it with pitha or vada. Ask what vegetables went into today’s pot. The answer gives you something to taste for.
sections.question: “How do you make your dalma, and what would you eat with it?”

sections.title: Let pakhala set a slower pace
sections.text: Rice in water opens another door into everyday Odia food. The tourism guide describes an overnight-fermented preparation, with fried vegetables and fish alongside. Preparations and accompaniments vary; ask what the kitchen is serving today. You do not need to order every dish to begin a conversation.
sections.question: “Is this preparation fermented, and which accompaniments come with it?”

sections.title: Leave room for the dark edge
sections.text: Chhena poda is a baked chhena sweet. Look at the browned edge before taking a bite; then notice the softer centre. A chef-authored Odisha Tourism account traces its origin to Nayagarh. Meeting a dish in Bhubaneswar is an invitation to follow it further into Odisha.
sections.question: Try the edge and the centre separately. Which would you save for the last bite?

closing: Choose a kitchen locally and ask what is available, what ingredients are used and what the meal costs. Tell the cook about dietary requirements before ordering. These are dishes to explore; we have not reviewed a restaurant or checked its current menu.
